summary: Macro backdrop for ags: headwind (score -2 across rates, dollar, Brazil real, risk, energy, China, breadth). rates +; dollar 0; brl −; risk 0; energy 0; china −; breadth −. Strongest ag/soft over the month: Cheese +15.2%; weakest: Oats -21.7%. Key releases ahead: US Average Hourly Earnings m/m (11-06 8:30 AM ET); US Non-Farm Employment Change (11-06 8:30 AM ET); US Unemployment Rate (11-06 8:30 AM ET).

sections.title: Rates
sections.text: US 10-year 4.90% (-41 bp in a month), 2-year 4.58% (-26 bp); 2s10s curve +32 bp (-15 bp in a month). Falling yields ease funding costs and support commodity investment flows. T-bill yield 4.03% sets the cost of carrying inventory.

sections.title: Dollar & farm currencies
sections.text: Dollar index 101.59 (-0.2% in a month, +3.4% YTD). USD/BRL 5.446 (+9.0% in a month): a weaker real encourages Brazilian farmer selling of soybeans, corn, sugar, coffee and cotton, pressuring world prices. USD/CNY 6.658 (-0.7%); USD/MXN 18.57 (+2.8%).

sections.title: Risk appetite
sections.text: S&P 500 -1.1% in a month (+12.3% YTD); VIX 16.8. Neutral risk backdrop.

sections.title: Energy
sections.text: WTI 89.53 $/bbl (+1.2% in a month), Brent 96.70, ULSD 4.275 $/gal (-3.3%), natural gas 2.93 (-13.9%). Crude little changed on the month. Natural gas drives nitrogen fertilizer costs for next year's corn.

sections.title: China & industrial demand
sections.text: Copper -3.4% in a month, Shanghai Composite -4.0%, Hang Seng +2.1%, yuan +0.7% vs USD. Soft China/industrial signals point to weaker import demand.

sections.title: Commodity breadth
sections.text: 7 of 33 commodities trade above their 50-day average (21%); S&P GSCI -5.4% in a month; gold -1.0%.

caveat: Directional channels from macro to ag prices are standard relationships, not signals tested on this desk; use as context.
